nodes.label: Streaming reporters (report.reporters, issue #12)
nodes.rationale: report.reporters can stream live cumulative metrics during the run to pluggable sinks, generalizing the historical report.url path; engine-owned keys (during_run, interval_ms, labels, max_series) sit next to use: while with: holds reporter-owned parameters. Lets perfscale stand in for k6 -o experimental-prometheus-rw with live Grafana dashboards.

nodes.label: std/report/serve@v1 reporter
nodes.rationale: The perfscale serve sink exposed as a reporter; the legacy report.url + during_run spelling still works and maps to this reporter. POSTs {samples, seq} batches to <url>/api/v1/metrics.

nodes.label: std/report/prometheus-rw@v1 reporter
nodes.rationale: Prometheus remote write sink using Snappy + protobuf; with.url targets the remote write endpoint; with.histogram selects classic (_bucket{le}) histograms (default, works everywhere) or native histograms (opt-in, backend feature required).

nodes.label: std/report/otel@v1 reporter
nodes.rationale: OTLP/gRPC sink (with.endpoint, e.g. an OpenTelemetry collector on :4317); exports exponential histograms with cumulative temporality and run start as start_time_unix_nano; counters/rates become monotonic cumulative sums, gauges stay gauges.

nodes.label: Bounded drop-oldest queue / backpressure policy
nodes.rationale: Each reporter has an independent bounded queue (with.max_pending, default 24); overflow drops the OLDEST snapshot/batch counted in perfscale_report_dropped_snapshots_total{reporter}. The engine never blocks on streaming: snapshots go over a bounded channel with try_send, so a slow or dead backend can never block the VUs, another reporter, or fail the run. Drop accounting is idempotent per run.

nodes.label: Batched delivery (with.batch_size)
nodes.rationale: Reporters batch by with.batch_size (default the run-level report.batch_size, 500); batches never exceed the batch size — an oversized snapshot splits into sequential batches, in order. One snapshot pump feeds all reporters at the fastest requested interval.

nodes.label: Retry with exponential backoff (with.retry)
nodes.rationale: Transient failures retry the same batch with exponential backoff (with.retry: max_attempts x backoff range like 1s..30s; Retry-After hint honored): network errors, HTTP 429/5xx, and transient gRPC statuses (Unavailable, ResourceExhausted, DeadlineExceeded). Any other 4xx or gRPC status is poison — dropped with a warning, never retried.

nodes.label: Synchronous final flush (with.final_timeout)
nodes.rationale: At run end the engine emits one terminal cumulative snapshot and the backlog coalesces to it — older batches are strict cumulative prefixes, so only the terminal snapshot is delivered. The flush is synchronous, bounded by with.final_timeout (default 30s); the CLI waits for it, and a failed or timed-out flush warns but never fails the load run.

nodes.label: Label merge: step > reporter > run
nodes.rationale: Labels come from three levels merged with priority step > reporter > run; values are scalars with ${{ inputs.* }} / ${{ env.* }} interpolation resolved once before the run. run_id and worker (shard index) are engine-set and rejected in user config; a step's own labels: apply only to that step's metrics.

nodes.label: Cardinality guard (max_series)
nodes.rationale: max_series (default 10000) caps each reporter's output series, classic buckets included; series beyond the limit are dropped deterministically (sorted order) and counted in perfscale_report_dropped_series_total{reporter}; the run continues. The report family's own counters are exempt.

nodes.label: report metric family (perfscale_report_*_total)
nodes.rationale: Per-run delivery counters (isolated across concurrent runs) registered as the report metric family — perfscale_report_dropped_series / _dropped_snapshots / _errors — exported to each backend as ..._total{reporter="<use>"} riding the snapshots; the terminal flush refreshes them before final export; also folded into the report@v1 document and summarized on stderr.

nodes.label: Bucketed histogram export, no client-side quantiles
nodes.rationale: Histograms stream bucketed, never as client-side quantiles, because quantiles from N workers cannot be merged while buckets can; backends compute correct cross-worker quantiles, e.g. histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(http_req_duration_bucket[1m]))). Durations export in seconds.

nodes.label: Cumulative snapshot model
nodes.rationale: All streamed values are cumulative since run start (HDR histograms and counters never reset), so a dropped snapshot only costs time resolution — the next snapshot restores every counter and histogram; consumers diff successive snapshots for per-window numbers. Snapshots carry {samples, seq} with a monotonically increasing seq reused across retries for dedup.

nodes.label: Platform/agent authenticated streaming
nodes.rationale: The CLI ships unauthenticated; the machine agent runs the same shipper with a Keycloak/machine token, stamping every sample with task_id and machine_id, feeding the run page, Metrics dashboard, Prometheus-compatible query API (/api/v1/integrations/prometheus) and Remote Write into the user's own Prometheus/Mimir.

hyperedges.label: Shared streaming delivery and failure policy
